programme.title: Genghis Khan: the Secret History of the Mongols

will show how, after a difficult childhood and captivity, he managed to gain power, unite the quarreling tribes, build an invincible army and subjugate all those who opposed him, including his former allies.Impressive conquests will be discussed, including:expansion into the West, campaigns against the neighboring Tangut people and the Chinese Jin Empire.The troops he commanded were known for the mobility of their cavalry, carrying out rapid attacks and retreats, and applying psychological pressure on their opponents.They used innovative techniques during sieges of even well-fortified cities.Genghis Khan became one of the most important figures in history, expanding his empire to unprecedented sizes.It stretched from the Pacific to the Caspian and Black Seas.The creators of the series are based on a new translation of the anonymous chronicle "The Secret History of the Mongols", which is the oldest known monument of writing of the steppe peoples of Central Asia A fascinating programme.title: Area 51: The CIA's Secret Files
programme.desc: The documentary presents the history of "Area 51", an air military base located in the desert near Las Vegas.The base was established in 1955, but its existence was officially confirmed only in 2013.This place is shrouded in legends because it is surrounded by a prohibited air zone of 1,140 square kilometers.The base developed programs that determined American dominance in military aviation from the Cold War to operations in Iraq and Afghanistan.Spy planes tested there were often mistaken for UFOs.The film features eyewitnesses to the creation of subsequent super-secret projects.Declassified CIA documents were used in the production.

programme.title: Chernobyl: Inside the Meltdown
programme.desc: On April 26, 1986, an explosion destroyed the fourth block of the Chernobyl power plant.The accident was caused by design defects in the reactor and errors during the safety test.It was the worst nuclear disaster in history.The explosion released 400 times more radiation than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.40 years after the tragedy, its consequences will be shown - from KGB activities to military operations in Ukraine.There will be plenty of witness accounts that will shed new light on the dramatic events.The speakers will include:a liquidator working on the roof of reactor 3, and journalist Wyatt Andrews, who was covering the information blackout in Moscow.
